screens.eyebrow: A practice plan for my clients · Burnout
screens.title: Four Weeks of Small Doses
screens.sub: Deepening what you started, one return at a time
screens.byline: Set-up takes about 15 minutes. After that, five to ten minutes on most days.

screens.title: How the plan works

blocks.p: On most days. That is the dose. More is not better here.
Nothing is lost. Coming back is the practice. This plan is about getting back, not about never leaving.
Use the section name at the top to jump to your week. Each week takes about four minutes to read and set up.
I give this plan to people when it fits. If it ever feels like one more thing to perform, tell me and we will change it.

screens.note: Finished Running on Fumes first? Good, this builds on it. If not, start there.

screens.text: Regulation is not staying calm. It is getting back.
screens.sub: Everyone floods sometimes, loud or quiet. Repair is the skill.

cards.p: One daily practice and two quick check-ins. You are collecting information.
Practice coming back when you notice you have left your window.
Make amends with yourself, and with the part that did the snapping.
Decide what stays, in the smallest version that still works.

screens.title: How the four weeks fit together
screens.summary: A walk through the plan, how to shrink it on a bad week, and what to bring to session.
bullets: How to shrink the plan when you are flooded or worn out

screens.title: Week 1: Notice

cards.p: The three-part toning breath, same time most days. After brushing your teeth or before the first coffee works well.
A ten-second check-in: revved up, in your window, or powered down? Just notice.
Pick one early signal: the first body sign that you are drifting toward flooding.

screens.intro: This week you are collecting information, not fixing anything.

screens.title: Week 1 tracker
screens.intro: Tick a box when you do it. Skipped days are just days.

screens.title: What did you notice this week?
screens.prompt: When did you drift away from your window, and what was happening just before? Was any part of you in charge then?
screens.placeholder: For example: Tuesday afternoon after the call, my Driver took over...

screens.title: Week 2: Return

cards.p: Cooling breath, then feet, seat, room. Notice how long it takes to settle. There is no right answer, only a number to be curious about.
Skip the cooling breath. Move a little, look around, say today's date. Try again later.
When something shifts, stay with it for one more breath and ask yourself what that is like.

screens.intro: Leaving your window is human. The return has four moves: notice you have left, name it ("a part of me is revved up"), choose a tool, then notice again what is even slightly different.

screens.title: Week 2 tracker
screens.intro: A return can be tiny. One slow breath out counts.

screens.title: Repair: what to do after you have left your window
screens.summary: Why repair matters more than perfection, and how to make amends with yourself and the part that snapped.

screens.title: Repair, in five moves
steps: Settle first. A few slow breaths. Repair goes badly when you are still flooded.
Say what happened plainly, with no verdict: "I snapped at Sam."
Thank the part that did it: "You were trying to protect me from something."
Ask what it needed. Listen for a word or a feeling, not a fix.
Offer that part one small thing, and the other person one small repair if there is one.
screens.eyebrow: For after you snapped, shut down, or went quiet
screens.note: Repair is not about being perfect. It is about not leaving yourself, or anyone else, alone in it.

screens.title: A repair
screens.prompt: Think of a time this week you left your window. What part of you was in charge, and what do you think it needed? What would you like to try next time?
screens.placeholder: For example: the Pleaser said yes to something I had no room for...

screens.title: Week 4: Rhythm

cards.p: What is the bad-day version? One breath counts.
Anything that feels like another thing to perform. Drop it, and tell me.

screens.intro: You will probably not keep doing everything forever. Good. Let's find the smallest version that still works.

screens.title: My rhythm
screens.prompt: What do you want to keep, shrink, or drop? What is your one-breath version for a bad day?
screens.placeholder: For example: keep the morning hum, shrink the check-ins to one a day...

screens.title: What to bring to session
screens.text: Four weeks of kindness to a nervous system.
items: What do we want to keep, shrink, or drop?
Which parts were most active, and what did they need?
Where did repair happen, even a little?
